Proposition
[Riccati comparison principle]

Source: petersen:page-0270

1. ch6:6.4.1aLet $\rho _1,\rho _2:(0,b)\to \mathbb {R}$ be smooth with \[ \dot\rho _1+\rho _1^2\le \dot\rho _2+\rho _2^2 , \] and let $F$ be an antiderivative of $\rho _1+\rho _2$ on $(0,b)$. Then $(\rho _2-\rho _1)e^{F}$ is nondecreasing on $(0,b)$; equivalently, for all $0<s\le t<b$, \[ \rho _2(t)-\rho _1(t)\ \ge \ \big(\rho _2(s)-\rho _1(s)\big) \exp \Big({-\int _s^t(\rho _1+\rho _2)}\Big). \]
Proof

\sketch For $G=(\rho _2-\rho _1)e^F$, $G'=(\dot\rho _2-\dot\rho _1+\rho _2^2-\rho _1^2)e^F\ge 0$. Integration gives the exponential comparison inequality.

□
